The idea comes from Andrey Karpathy, OpenAI co-founder, and it pulled 25 million views: use AI less as a code writer and more as a second brain.

How it works: aim Claude Code at a folder and toss in anything - an article, a transcript, a PDF. Claude reads it, connects it to what's already there and files it into a wiki that keeps growing. Every new source makes the whole thing sharper, like compound interest.

Quick setup:
- Install Obsidian, make a vault, open it inside Claude Code
- Paste in Karpathy's wiki file and ask Claude to build it
- You get three folders: raw for inputs, wiki for Claude's pages, plus a CLAUDE file that runs the show
- Put a new file in raw and tell Claude: "ingest this"
- Query everything you've ever saved

About 5 minutes of setup and no more blank chats. Full guide in the article below.

CLAUDE FORGETS YOU EVERY F*CKING SESSION

Anthropic's own docs say it straight: every Claude Code session starts with a fresh context window.

Your folder layout, your naming rules, every "no, not like that". Gone the second the session ends.

The fix is 4 memory layers. Most people set up 1, stuff it to 600 lines and decide AI memory doesn't work.

Check yours in 5 seconds:

/context

If CLAUDE.md isn't listed under "Memory files", Claude has never read a single rule in it.

here's the split:

→ CLAUDE.md is the map. You write it, it loads every session, keep it under 200 lines
→ .claude/rules/ are reflexes. Add paths: and a rule loads only when Claude touches a matching file
→ skills are playbooks. They load only when you call them or the task needs them
→ auto memory is the diary. Claude writes it from your corrections, the first 200 lines load every session

two myths everyone repeats:

→ CLAUDE.md is not the system prompt. It lands as a user message right after it
→ "never do X" in CLAUDE.md is a wish. Memory is context, not enforcement. A PreToolUse hook is the only real never

You write the map. Claude writes the diary. A hook says no.

the full tree
> CLAUDE.md under 200 lines, HTML comments cost 0 tokens
> .claude/rules/people.md with paths: people/**, loads on touch
> .claude/skills/weekly-review/SKILL.md, loads on call
> auto memory: say "remember ...", open it with /memory
> PreToolUse hook for every hard never
> /compact re-reads CLAUDE.md from disk, rules typed only in chat die
> /doctor prompt-audit finds rules that contradict each other (v2.1.283+)

paste this into Claude Code ↓

"Set up a second brain in this folder from the tree above:
1. Create notes/, people/, projects/, drafts/ and a CLAUDE.md under 200 lines: where things live, lowercase-with-hyphens, one topic per file.
2. Move every folder-specific rule into .claude/rules/ with a paths: field.
3. Turn every repeated routine into a skill in .claude/skills/.
4. Put anything that must never happen into a PreToolUse hook, not into CLAUDE.md.
Show me the file tree before you create anything. Don't invent content for my notes."

I FOUND 8 GITHUB REPOS THAT CAN SERIOUSLY UPGRADE YOUR CLAUDE OPUS 5.5 ANIMATIONS.

I’ve been seeing some incredible animations made with Opus 5.5.

But here’s what many people are missing:

It’s not just about writing better prompts.

There are ready-made animation styles, open-source projects, and workflows that can take your results to another level.

And most of them are completely FREE.

I dug around and found 8 GitHub repos worth bookmarking.

1. awesome-opus5-5-videos

A massive collection of animations created with Claude Opus 5.5.

3D scenes, motion graphics, and video examples, including the prompts behind some of the best results.

https://t.co/tc3yreR9sC…

2. lemo-opuscar

One of the most practical repos on this list.

It includes 66 different animation and video styles designed for Claude Code.

Pick a style, adapt it to your idea, and generate animations directly with code. No AI video model required.

https://t.co/4Aat6iJhI7…

3. pdoom-video

A complete music video project created entirely with code.

Explore music-synchronized animations, karaoke effects, 3D visuals, and the 4K rendering workflow.

https://t.co/r3DOwH5Sup…

4. PDoomVideo

Another music video project created for the same song as the previous repo.

Compare both projects and see how the same music can produce completely different visual storytelling.

https://t.co/uJODuulvxh…

5. mg-styles-15

15 different motion graphics styles.

Each one includes a 10-second animation example, the original prompt, and the source code.

Perfect for YouTube visuals, animated statistics, and product introductions.

https://t.co/FQdr93MFK5…

6. ClaudeAnimationBase

A starter project for creating cartoon-style character animations.

Includes 31 different facial expressions, character movements, and an animation development guide.

https://t.co/C2iM6hTIhW…

7. awesome-claude-5-5-videos

Another archive of animations made with Claude.

You can explore original source files, tools, examples, and the workflows used to create them.

https://t.co/thFMUVrWRA…

8. opus-video-prompts

A collection of 54 video production examples and prompts you can adapt for your own projects.

Covers motion graphics, animation, and code-based video creation.

https://t.co/QCvaMQ1y05…

You don’t have to figure everything out from scratch.

Some of these repos can be set up by simply giving Claude Code or Codex the GitHub link and asking it to install the project.

Others let you study the actual source code, prompts, and finished examples.

I’d start with lemo-opuscar and awesome-opus5-5-videos.

I’m also sharing an example made with Lemo-Opuscar so you can see what’s possible.

🎬 Video: Aura — Hear the Light

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

I FOUND 8 GITHUB REPOS THAT CAN SERIOUSLY UPGRADE YOUR CLAUDE OPUS 5.5 ANIMATIONS.

I’ve been seeing some incredible animations made with Opus 5.5.

But here’s what many people are missing:

It’s not just about writing better prompts.

There are ready-made animation styles, open-source projects, and workflows that can take your results to another level.

And most of them are completely FREE.

I dug around and found 8 GitHub repos worth bookmarking.

1. awesome-opus5-5-videos

A massive collection of animations created with Claude Opus 5.5.

3D scenes, motion graphics, and video examples, including the prompts behind some of the best results.

https://t.co/tc3yreR9sC…

2. lemo-opuscar

One of the most practical repos on this list.

It includes 66 different animation and video styles designed for Claude Code.

Pick a style, adapt it to your idea, and generate animations directly with code. No AI video model required.

https://t.co/4Aat6iJhI7…

3. pdoom-video

A complete music video project created entirely with code.

Explore music-synchronized animations, karaoke effects, 3D visuals, and the 4K rendering workflow.

https://t.co/r3DOwH5Sup…

4. PDoomVideo

Another music video project created for the same song as the previous repo.

Compare both projects and see how the same music can produce completely different visual storytelling.

https://t.co/uJODuulvxh…

5. mg-styles-15

15 different motion graphics styles.

Each one includes a 10-second animation example, the original prompt, and the source code.

Perfect for YouTube visuals, animated statistics, and product introductions.

https://t.co/FQdr93MFK5…

6. ClaudeAnimationBase

A starter project for creating cartoon-style character animations.

Includes 31 different facial expressions, character movements, and an animation development guide.

https://t.co/C2iM6hTIhW…

7. awesome-claude-5-5-videos

Another archive of animations made with Claude.

You can explore original source files, tools, examples, and the workflows used to create them.

https://t.co/thFMUVrWRA…

8. opus-video-prompts

A collection of 54 video production examples and prompts you can adapt for your own projects.

Covers motion graphics, animation, and code-based video creation.

https://t.co/QCvaMQ1y05…

You don’t have to figure everything out from scratch.

Some of these repos can be set up by simply giving Claude Code or Codex the GitHub link and asking it to install the project.

Others let you study the actual source code, prompts, and finished examples.

I’d start with lemo-opuscar and awesome-opus5-5-videos.

I’m also sharing an example made with Lemo-Opuscar so you can see what’s possible.

🎬 Video: Aura — Hear the Light

Project: Lemo-Opuscar | Claude Opus 5.5
